question: Alexander and Porus fought on the banks of which of the following rivers?
solution:
The correct answer is __**Jhelum**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] __Key Points__

__
 
• Alexander the Great and King Porus fought the famous Battle of the Hydaspes in 326 BC.
 
• The battle took place on the banks of the Jhelum River, which was known as the Hydaspes in ancient times.
 
• This battle was significant because it marked Alexander’s attempt to expand his empire into the Indian subcontinent.
 
• Despite being heavily outnumbered, Alexander's army managed to defeat Porus, who was known for his valor and bravery.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Alexander the Great**

 
 
• Alexander III of Macedon, commonly known as Alexander the Great, was a king of the ancient Greek kingdom of Macedon.
 
• He was born in Pella in 356 BC and succeeded his father Philip II to the throne at the age of 20.
 
• By the age of 30, he had created one of the largest empires in history, stretching from Greece to northwestern India.
 
• He is considered one of history's most successful military commanders.
 
 
 
• **Porus**
 
 
• King Porus, also known as Purushottama, was an ancient Indian king whose territory spanned the region between the Jhelum and Chenab rivers (in present-day Punjab, Pakistan).
 
• He is known for his courageous stand against Alexander the Great in the Battle of the Hydaspes.
 
• Despite his defeat, Alexander was impressed by Porus’s bravery and allowed him to retain his kingdom and even granted him more territory.
 
 
 
• **Battle of the Hydaspes**
 
 
• The Battle of the Hydaspes was fought between Alexander the Great and King Porus in 326 BC.
 
• The battle took place on the banks of the Jhelum River (then known as Hydaspes) in what is now Punjab, Pakistan.
 
• It is one of the most significant battles fought by Alexander during his campaign to conquer the Achaemenid Persian Empire and expand his empire into the Indian subcontinent.
 
• Despite the challenging conditions, including a monsoon and the river’s strong currents, Alexander’s tactical genius led to his victory over Porus.
